item.title: Tráfego marítimo pelo Estreito de Ormuz segue abaixo da média de 10 dias, mostram dados
item.description: Cinco navios de carga transitaram pelo Estreito de Ormuz na terça-feira, um número praticamente inalterado em relação ao dia anterior, mas bem abaixo da média de 15 navios nos últimos 10 dias, segundo dados preliminares de tráfego marítimo divulgados nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Mohi Narayan
item.content:encoded: Cinco navios de carga transitaram pelo Estreito de Ormuz na terça-feira, um número praticamente inalterado em relação ao dia anterior, mas bem abaixo da média de 15 navios nos últimos 10 dias, segundo dados preliminares de tráfego marítimo divulgados nesta quarta-feira. Dois petroleiros transportando gás liquefeito de petróleo e um petroleiro transportando betume saíram do Golfo Pérsico pelo estreito, enquanto dois petroleiros de produtos petroquímicos vazios entraram na via navegável vindos do Golfo de Omã, segundo dados iniciais da empresa de rastreamento de navios Kpler, divulgados às 01h08 (horário de Brasília). Na segunda-feira, quatro navios de carga transitaram pela via navegável, segundo os dados. Os números podem sofrer alterações, já que alguns navios costumam desligar seus transponders de localização durante a viagem. As travessias pelo estreito de Bab el-Mandeb, outro importante ponto de estrangulamento marítimo no Oriente Médio, também permaneceram praticamente inalteradas, com 31 navios de commodities contra 29 no dia anterior, segundo dados da Kpler, mas em linha com a média de 10 dias. O Irã afirmou ter retomado as discussões com Omã sobre a gestão do Estreito de Ormuz em meio à crescente pressão econômica do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. As duas partes afirmaram na terça-feira que haviam estudado a criação de um corredor marítimo conjunto temporário e concordaram em remover as minas da via navegável. “Qualquer acordo entre essas duas partes não significa que veremos a normalização dos fluxos de petróleo por esse importante ponto de estrangulamento”, afirmou a ING Economics em uma nota. “Provavelmente, seria necessário que os EUA suspendessem o bloqueio aos portos iranianos e flexibilizassem as sanções contra o Irã antes de observarmos qualquer avanço em direção à normalização.” (Reportagem de Mohi Narayan)

item.title: Minério de ferro sobe com tufão Narra interrompendo rotas marítimas
item.description: Os contratos futuros de minério de ferro subiram nesta quarta-feira, depois que o tufão Narra interrompeu as rotas marítimas no Mar do Sul da China, reduzindo a oferta e elevando os custos de frete.
item.dc:creator: Emily Yong
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de minério de ferro subiram nesta quarta-feira, depois que o tufão Narra interrompeu as rotas marítimas no Mar do Sul da China, reduzindo a oferta e elevando os custos de frete. O contrato de minério de ferro para janeiro mais negociado na Bolsa de Mercadorias de Dalian (DCE) na China fechou o pregão diurno com alta de 0,49%, a 720 iuanes (US$107,14) por tonelada, ampliando os ganhos pela quarta sessão consecutiva. A referência de minério de ferro para setembro na Bolsa de Cingapura subia 1,04%, para US$98,15 por tonelada. O tufão Narra interrompeu as rotas no Mar do Sul da China, prejudicando o abastecimento e elevando os custos de frete, afirmou um analista de mercado com sede na Malásia. Custos de frete mais elevados tendem a sustentar os preços do minério de ferro transportado por via marítima. As áreas costeiras e regiões do sul da China estão se preparando para dias de [USN:L4N44N05R TEXT:"chuvas intensas"], com dezenas de milhares de pessoas evacuadas à medida que o tufão Narra avança para o interior e outra tempestade se aproxima da costa leste do país. No entanto, os ganhos nos preços do minério foram limitados, já que a produção das siderúrgicas desacelerou em meio a perdas crescentes, enquanto os estoques das usinas permanecem relativamente altos, afirmaram analistas da corretora chinesa Everbright Futures em nota. As principais empresas siderúrgicas produziram 1,97 milhão de toneladas de aço bruto em meados de agosto, com a produção média diária caindo 0,4% em relação ao período anterior de 10 dias, enquanto os estoques de aço subiram 6,7%, para 18,33 milhões de toneladas, de acordo com dados da Associação Chinesa de Ferro e Aço. Os estoques portuários em sete grandes portos da Austrália e do Brasil aumentaram 647 mil toneladas, para 13,41 milhões de toneladas, na semana encerrada em 23 de agosto, permanecendo acima do nível médio para esta época do ano, segundo dados da consultoria Mysteel. (Reportagem de Emily Ou Yong)

item.title: Tereos prevê produção de açúcar da UE no menor nível em 38 anos, em meio a clima adverso
item.description: A produtora francesa de açúcar Tereos prevê que o calor extremo e a seca deste verão reduzam a produtividade da beterraba sacarina de seus produtores em mais de 20% em comparação com o ano passado, contribuindo para que a produção de açúcar da União Europeia atinja o menor nível em 38 anos, informou a empresa nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A produtora francesa de açúcar Tereos prevê que o calor extremo e a seca deste verão reduzam a produtividade da beterraba sacarina de seus produtores em mais de 20% em comparação com o ano passado, contribuindo para que a produção de açúcar da União Europeia atinja o menor nível em 38 anos, informou a empresa nesta quarta-feira. A beterraba-sacarina está entre as culturas de verão, como [USN:L1N44L0DN TEXT:"o milho"] e [USN:L8N44L19Z TEXT:"a batata"], que foram gravemente afetadas pelas condições climáticas extremas na Europa. A Tereos informou que a produtividade da beterraba de seus produtores franceses também deve ficar cerca de 15% abaixo da média das últimas cinco safras. Em resposta à safra afetada pelo clima, a Tereos planeja encurtar sua campanha de produção de açúcar em suas oito fábricas francesas para 100 dias, em média, em comparação com 130 dias no ano passado, informou em comunicado. A Tereos também adiará o início da campanha para permitir que as plantações de beterraba possam, potencialmente, ganhar algum rendimento. A Tereos afirmou que os preços do açúcar estão se recuperando após dois anos de queda, o que havia levado a [USN:L8N43X0UY TEXT:"lucros menores"] para a empresa e para seus concorrentes europeus. A redução esperada da oferta e a diminuição do plantio devem ajudar o mercado a se reequilibrar. “Hoje, estamos vendo os primeiros sinais de um aumento nos preços de venda, o que deve permitir que o setor retorne a um nível mais equilibrado de desempenho”, afirmou Pierre-Henri Dietz, diretor comercial da Tereos, no comunicado. Em comunicado conjunto divulgado na terça-feira, a Tereos e outros [USN:L6N44M0II TEXT:"produtores franceses"] alertaram que a produção de beterraba sacarina poderia ficar mais de 20% abaixo da média, com o impacto do calor e da seca agravado pela pressão de pragas e doenças. (Reportagem de Gus Trompiz)

item.title: Prince Harry and family due back in UK as they return from US, BBC reports
item.description: Prince Harry and his family were due to arrive back in Britain on Wednesday, the BBC reported, days after it was revealed the couple were moving back six years after quitting royal duties and relocating to the United States.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Prince Harry and his family were due to arrive back in Britain on Wednesday, the BBC reported, days after it was revealed the couple were moving back six years after quitting royal duties and relocating to the United States. Last week, Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, [USN:L8N44H0TT TEXT:"surprised even their close family"] when it was disclosed that they would relocate from California to somewhere outside London for what was described as an extended period of time. Their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, will start school in Britain in September. Precise details have not been disclosed about where they will live, other than it will not be a royal residence, nor the school the children will attend. The BBC said it understood they would be flying in from California privately on Wednesday. There was no immediate comment from Harry's spokesperson.

item.title: Department store chain Kohl's misses quarterly sales estimates amid cautious spending
item.description: Kohl's missed Wall Street estimates for second-quarter sales on Wednesday, as cautious consumer spending on discretionary items offset gains from the high-end department chain's turnaround push, sending its shares down about 5% before the bell.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kohl's (KSS.N) missed Wall Street estimates for second-quarter sales on Wednesday, as cautious consumer spending on discretionary items offset gains from the high-end department chain's turnaround push, sending its shares down about 5% before the bell. The company, however, raised its annual profit forecast after benefiting from $150 million tariff refunds received during the reported quarter. Kohl's also said it will resume its about $100 million share repurchase program this year. U.S. consumer sentiment deteriorated in [USN:AQN2MET4Z TEXT:"August"] and retail sales fell for the first time in nine months in July , underscoring an increasingly [USN:L4N44H0Z5 TEXT:""selective""] shopping trend among middle- and lower-income households in the face of stubborn inflation, even as wealthier shoppers remain resilient. This cautious behavior of consumers when spending on nice-to-have items, including apparel and home goods, has been weighing on businesses from high-end store owners such as Kohl's to off-price retailers like [USN:L6N44G0P7 TEXT:"TJX."] Kohl's quarterly revenue fell 0.9% to $3.32 billion from a year ago, compared with analysts' estimates of about a 0.1% decline to $3.35 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. The company now expects fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.80 to $2.40 per share, compared with its prior forecast of $1.00 to $1.60.

item.title: Grecia finalizzerà acquisto due fregate italiane a settembre - min. Difesa
item.description: Il mese prossimo la Grecia concluderà un accordo per l’acquisto delle prime due fregate della classe Bergamini dall’Italia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Il mese prossimo la Grecia concluderà un accordo per l’acquisto delle prime due fregate della classe Bergamini dall’Italia. Lo ha detto il ministero della Difesa greco in relazione al processo di modernizzazione delle forze armate del Paese membro Nato. L'anno scorso la Grecia aveva raggiunto un accordo per l’acquisto di quattro fregate usate della classe Bergamini dall’Italia. L’8 settembre il ministro Crosetto e la controparte greca Nikos Dendias firmeranno un "accordo di attuazione" in cui saranno delineati i termini legali, finanziari e tecnici per l’acquisto delle prime due fregate, secondo quanto riportato in un comunicato del ministero della Difesa greco. La Grecia, che spende quasi il 3,5% del Pil per la difesa – percentuale superiore a quella di molti altri Paesi Nato – prevede di spendere circa 28 miliardi di euro nell’ambito di un piano pluriennale di difesa entro il 2036, nel tentativo di tenere testa alla Turchia, sua rivale storica.

item.title: Los trabajadores de Airbus en España reanudan la huelga tras rechazar una oferta salarial
item.description: Miles de trabajadores de Airbus en España han reanudado esta semana las medidas de huelga tras rechazar la última oferta salarial y la propuesta de mediación de la empresa, informaron los sindicatos este miércoles, antes de una nueva reunión de mediación prevista para el jueves.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Miles de trabajadores de Airbus (AIR.PA) en España han reanudado esta semana las medidas de huelga tras rechazar la última oferta salarial y la propuesta de mediación de la empresa, informaron los sindicatos este miércoles, antes de una nueva reunión de mediación prevista para el jueves. Los sindicatos afirmaron que alrededor del 90% de los trabajadores con derecho a participar en el paro del martes se sumaron a la huelga, que describieron como el inicio de una huelga indefinida tras 22 días de paros en julio. Los sindicatos franceses informados sobre el conflicto han señalado que los tres sindicatos españoles en huelga representan alrededor del 40% de los aproximadamente 14.000 empleados de Airbus España. No ha sido posible confirmar de forma independiente el número de trabajadores que participaron. La huelga se convocó después de que los trabajadores votaran en asambleas celebradas en las distintas plantas para rechazar una propuesta salarial y de condiciones laborales presentada por la empresa en una sesión de mediación el viernes. Los sindicatos afirmaron que la oferta carecía de plazos concretos y compromisos financieros, y que dejaba pendientes cuestiones clave como las vacaciones, la flexibilidad horaria y el transporte. Airbus, que se encuentra bajo presión para cumplir su objetivo anual de entrega de 870 aviones, ha congelado las contrataciones previstas en España mientras dure la huelga, según Alfonso Mora, presidente del comité de empresa de Airbus en España. Airbus no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Los representantes sindicales de UGT y CGT afirmaron que el paro ya había ralentizado la producción militar y comercial y que dificultaría que la empresa cumpliera su objetivo de entregas. Airbus dijo la semana pasada que las interrupciones en las funciones administrativas y de apoyo aún no habían afectado a la producción. Los trabajadores reclaman aumentos salariales indexados a la inflación, el restablecimiento de los acuerdos previos de teletrabajo y prestaciones por baja por enfermedad. Airbus ya ha suavizado sus planes de reducir el teletrabajo tras las protestas de julio, permitiendo al personal seguir trabajando desde casa una media de dos días a la semana, informó Reuters la semana pasada. Las ocho plantas de Airbus en España fabrican aviones de transporte militar y piezas para aviones comerciales y satélites.

item.title: Narrow majority of Icelanders back EU membership talks, poll shows ahead of referendum
item.description: A narrow majority of Icelanders support restarting negotiations on joining the European Union in a nationwide referendum set for Saturday, according to a new opinion poll, down slightly from the previous survey.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A narrow majority of Icelanders support restarting negotiations on joining the European Union in a [USN:L6N44A0QY TEXT:"nationwide referendum"] set for Saturday, according to a new opinion poll, down slightly from the previous survey. The [USN:L8N42418Y TEXT:"August 29 ballot"] is not a vote on membership itself and any deal with the EU would require Iceland to hold a second referendum on whether to join the bloc based on the terms agreed in the negotiations. The August 21-25 survey of 1,019 people by polling agency Maskina showed 51.3% of respondents support holding negotiations with Brussels on joining the bloc, while 48.7% are opposed, Icelandic daily Visir reported. The gap between the two sides has narrowed further since an August 13 poll, when 52.2% said they backed restarting the talks while 47.8% said they opposed them. Reykjavik abandoned EU membership talks in 2013 after four years of negotiations, but a rise in the cost of living and the war in Ukraine are among the factors in recent years that have rekindled Iceland's interest in joining the 27-nation bloc. [USN:L1N3YG0BO TEXT:"Repeated threats"] by U.S. President Donald Trump to [USN:L1N3Z90CF TEXT:"annex Greenland"], located between Iceland and the United States, have also revived interest in joining the EU. Iceland is already part of the European single market, the Schengen open-border travel zone, and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) alongside Norway and Liechtenstein, but has no formal influence on how the EU evolves. EU membership would give Iceland [USN:L8N44A143 TEXT:"a direct say"] in decision-making via institutions such as the European Commission, the Council of Ministers and the European Parliament. It would also involve Iceland joining the EU's customs union and offer the option of adopting the euro. In the event of a 'yes' vote in Saturday's referendum, a foreign ministry memo estimates that accession talks could start by the end of 2026 and be concluded within 18 to 24 months.

item.title: Taxas de juros precisam subir mais devido aos riscos de inflação, diz membro do BCE à Bloomberg
item.description: Isabel Schnabel, membro do Conselho do Banco Central Europeu, afirmou que as taxas de juros devem subir ainda mais uma vez que o conflito no Oriente Médio se prolonga e a força da economia da zona do euro representa riscos de alta para a inflação, em entrevista à Bloomberg News publicada nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Isabel Schnabel, membro do Conselho do Banco Central Europeu, afirmou que as taxas de juros devem subir ainda mais uma vez que o conflito no Oriente Médio se prolonga e a força da economia da zona do euro representa riscos de alta para a inflação, em entrevista à Bloomberg News publicada nesta quarta-feira. “Com a taxa de juros atual, é improvável que a inflação retorne à meta no médio prazo e, portanto, será necessário um aperto monetário adicional”, disse Schnabel à Bloomberg. Três fontes informaram à Reuters na terça-feira que as autoridades do BCE estavam inclinadas a um aumento dos juros em sua reunião de setembro para conter o impacto inflacionário da guerra no Irã, mas demonstram pouca disposição para sinalizar um aperto monetário adicional além disso. Schnabel disse que a alta dos preços ao consumidor provavelmente ultrapassará 2% por um “período prolongado” devido aos elevados custos da energia, e que agir apenas quando isso se refletir nos salários deixaria as autoridades “atrasadas em relação à curva”. O BCE elevou os custos dos empréstimos pela primeira vez em quase três anos em junho para evitar que o aumento nos preços da energia devido à guerra se espalhasse pela economia. Schnabel afirmou que os mercados “parecem compreender muito bem nossa função de reação”, sem especificar até que ponto os custos dos empréstimos provavelmente subirão. (Reportagem de Anusha Shah em Bengaluru)

item.title: Pelo menos 14 bebês morrem em incêndio em hospital de Islamabad
item.description: Pelo menos 14 bebês morreram em um incêndio em um hospital público na capital do Paquistão, Islamabad, nesta quarta-feira, informou o primeiro-ministro, enquanto o ministro da Saúde atribuiu a tragédia a uma explosão na ala de neonatologia.
item.dc:creator: Rick Noack, Akhtar Soomro, Asif Shahzad
item.content:encoded: Pelo menos 14 bebês morreram em um incêndio em um hospital público na capital do Paquistão, Islamabad, nesta quarta-feira, informou o primeiro-ministro, enquanto o ministro da Saúde atribuiu a tragédia a uma explosão na ala de neonatologia. O incêndio começou por volta das 7h (horário local) no Instituto de Ciências Médicas do Paquistão, no terceiro andar da ala de saúde materno-infantil do hospital, informou a emissora Geo TV, que estimou o número de mortos em 15. “O incêndio começou após uma explosão em (um) aparelho de ar-condicionado”, disse o ministro da Saúde, Mustafa Kamal, à Geo TV, acrescentando que a grande quantidade de oxigênio na ala contribuiu para a propagação do fogo. O incidente está entre os incêndios hospitalares mais mortais dos últimos anos no país, onde a assistência médica pública é subsidiada, mas as instalações carecem de recursos e estão sobrecarregadas. Órgãos de fiscalização têm criticado frequentemente as instalações estatais por má gestão. Imagens de televisão mostraram uma ala destruída e enegrecida, com equipamentos espalhados e fumaça ainda subindo. Havia 16 recém-nascidos na ala quando o incêndio começou, um dos quais foi resgatado, informou a Geo. A ala foi posteriormente isolada, disse uma testemunha da Reuters. As imagens mostravam mulheres devastadas pela dor sentadas no chão do lado de fora do hospital. Uma delas era Javeria, que perdeu seu recém-nascido no incêndio. “Era uma ala de ginecologia... não havia médico, nem enfermeira”, disse ela, acrescentando que os corpos das crianças foram levados “em caixas” e que as mulheres não puderam vê-los. “Não é a vontade de Deus… eu não aceito isso”, afirmou. Kamal negou as acusações de que não havia funcionários ou médicos presentes no momento do incêndio. O primeiro-ministro Shehbaz Sharif suspendeu o secretário de Saúde por causa do incidente, informou seu gabinete, horas depois de ele ter ordenado uma investigação. O prédio que abrigava a enfermaria “não tinha segurança contra incêndio, nem saídas adequadas. Todas as portas estavam fechadas; apenas uma porta estava (aberta) para que pudéssemos visitar nossos filhos”, disse Mudasir, que também perdeu seu filho. Javeria e Mudasir forneceram apenas seus primeiros nomes. O Instituto de Ciências Médicas do Paquistão, para onde o ex-primeiro-ministro Imran Khan foi levado brevemente para um exame médico na semana passada, está localizado no centro de Islamabad e é um dos principais hospitais públicos da cidade, que tem cerca de 1,1 milhão de habitantes.

item.title: Workplace diversity data lives!
item.description: The opinions expressed in this column are those of the author, a correspondent for Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Ross Kerber
item.content:encoded: The opinions expressed in this column are those of the author, a correspondent for Reuters. "You can't manage what you can't measure," goes the business aphorism at the heart of countless corporate diversity discussions. Soon there may be fewer measurements to manage. Since 1966, companies have detailed to the U.S. government their workforce demographics by job title, sex and race, a requirement stemming from the Civil Rights Act of 1964. Lately many companies made the information public [USN:KBN2431JX TEXT:"under pressure"] from investment activists. This data would no longer be collected, according to plans by the U.S. agency that enforces laws banning workplace discrimination, known as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. Two of its three members were nominated by U.S. President Donald Trump and they voted in July to scrap the practice [USN:L1N43N0RQ TEXT:"known as EEO-1 reporting"] based on the forms that companies with 100 or more employees currently submit. The change is no surprise, and connects to culture-war issues. The Trump-aligned Heritage Foundation's Project 2025 policy document called for ending the data collection lest it "be used to support a charge of discrimination... This could lead to racial quotas to remedy alleged race discrimination," the document states. "Crudely categorizing employees by race or ethnicity fails to recognize the diversity of the American workforce and forces individuals into categories that do not fully reflect their racial and ethnic heritage," reads the document, in a section written by Jonathan Berry, now Trump's Solicitor of Labor. You might expect executives to welcome less reporting. But business leaders want to move with care, according to some of the comment letters on the proposed change that were due on August 24. Marc Freedman, a vice president for the U.S. Chamber of Commerce , the top business lobbying group, wrote that it supports ending EEO-1 reporting but said employers often use workforce demographic data "for wholly lawful, business-related, and quality-control purposes" such as pay reviews or legal compliance. It asked the EEOC for more clarity on when businesses can collect and use such data. "Employers will want to know they can continue to collect this data consistent with the administration's [USN:FWN40E0ZQ TEXT:"concerns"] around DEI activities," Freedman said in an interview. The National Retail Federation similarly praised the end of EEO-1 reporting but asked the commission to "recognize employers may continue to collect, retain, analyze, and use workforce demographic data for lawful compliance, self-audit, pay equity, validation, litigation defense, investigation response, and compliance with applicable state and local laws." "DATA IS NOT THE PROBLEM" Leaders of The Institute for Workplace Equality, whose members include large employers like Charles Schwab, (SCHW.N) Coca-Cola, (KO.N) Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Northrop Grumman, (NOC.N) went further and said there is no evidence companies have used the data to create quotas, as critics fear. They suggested officials look to different reforms. "The data is not the problem. Eliminating it does not eliminate discrimination. It eliminates our ability to see it," wrote Barbara Moskowitz, the institute's director. Of the 2,580 comments shown on Regulations.gov as of Tuesday, 88% opposed the proposed change, according to a random sampling of 150 comments conducted by Donald Tomaskovic-Devey, a University of Massachusetts sociology professor. In an interview, Tomaskovic-Devey said the EEOC's data has become the key measure for judging how companies promote equal opportunity in employment and pay equity. He made similar points in a comment letter co-signed by 44 other academics. Without the data, "The EEOC will be effectively flying blind in its reporting and regulatory obligations," they wrote. "There's nothing about this that was mobilized by business opposition to the EEOC. This is not normal politics," Tomaskovic-Devey said. Jenny Yang, who was EEOC Chair from 2014 until 2017, said executives worry their long-established human resources reviews of areas like hiring or pay equity could make them targets for the administration, given rhetoric like that of Project 2025. Businesses "want to be able to continue to evaluate their own practices," she said. RACIAL STEREOTYPES AT WORK A representative for the EEOC did not address what if any rulemaking changes might result from the comments received. EEOC representative Victor Chen provided a statement from Chair Andrea Lucas accompanying the proposed rulemaking, which made no mention of using demographic data in a positive manner. Instead she cited potential harms from the current demographic reporting requirement. These include pushing employers to prevent discrimination only against minorities and women, promoting racial stereotyping at work, and "incentivizing employers to unlawfully treat employees differently based on race or sex in order to 'correct' perceived imbalances in employee representation." Meredith Benton, principal of Whistle Stop Capital, a research firm that has supported clients' shareholder resolutions seeking diversity data disclosure, said whatever the EEOC decides, companies she speaks with will keep tracking diversity data. Executives want it both to manage their workforces and as a defense against future charges of discrimination. "That part of the story hasn't changed," she said in an interview.

item.title: TSX futures flat as investors weigh National Bank of Canada's results, trade war
item.description: Futures linked to Canada's stock index were subdued on Wednesday as investors weighed positive quarterly results from National Bank of Canada, alongside the ongoing trade war with the U.S.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Futures linked to Canada's stock index were subdued on Wednesday as investors weighed positive quarterly results from National Bank of Canada, alongside the ongoing trade war with the U.S. Futures on the S&P/TSX index were flat at 2,164.20 points at 6:40 a.m. ET, after the benchmark index logged a record high in the previous session. National Bank of Canada (NA.TO) [USN:L4N44N0OS TEXT:"reported"] a rise in third-quarter profit, driven by a robust performance in its wealth management segment. The latest results add to a series of [USN:L6N44M0JK TEXT:"stronger-than-expected"] quarterly results by Bank of Montreal (BMO.TO) and Bank of Nova Scotia (BNS.TO) on Tuesday, which helped the TSX [USN:L6N44M10B TEXT:"notch"] a record high. Traders kept an eye on the ongoing trade war with the U.S. after Canada [USN:L6N44M0TW TEXT:"hit back"] with retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion worth of U.S. annual imports, matching Washington's latest duties dollar-for-dollar. The counter-tariffs on U.S. goods take effect on September 8 and impose duties of 15%, 25% and 50% across around 700 products imported from south of the border, a government statement mentioned. Meanwhile, gold prices slipped as traders awaited U.S. inflation data due at 8:30 a.m. ET, which could offer clues on the Federal Reserve's outlook on interest rates. Spot gold shed 0.8%, while silver slipped 0.2%. Oil prices fell more than 2% as [USN:L8N44M1SQ TEXT:"talks"] between Iran and Oman revived hopes that the Strait of Hormuz could reopen. Brent crude futures shed 2.9%, while West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 2.7%. item.title: Futures fiacchi in attesa trimestrale Nvidia, dati inflazione
item.description: I futures sui principali indici azionari Usa sono sostanzialmente invariati mentre gli investitori mantengono un approccio cauto in vista della trimestrale di Nvidia e dell'atteso dato sull’inflazione che potrebbe influenzare le aspettative sui tassi di interesse.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: I futures sui principali indici azionari Usa sono sostanzialmente invariati mentre gli investitori mantengono un approccio cauto in vista della trimestrale di Nvidia e dell'atteso dato sull’inflazione che potrebbe influenzare le aspettative sui tassi di interesse. ** I dati sulle spese per i consumi personali (Pce), l’indicatore di inflazione preferito dalla Federal Reserve, dovrebbe mostrare un aumento delle pressioni sui prezzi al 3,6% a luglio. Nel corso della giornata è prevista anche una seconda stima sulla crescita economica. ** Secondo i dati Lseg, i trader prezzano già un rialzo dei tassi di 25 punti base nel 2026, anche se una lettura sull'inflazione al consumo in linea con le attese ha ridotto le probabilità di un rialzo già a settembre. ** Un altro aspetto cruciale per i mercati sono i risultati trimestrali di Nvidia (NVDA.O) , ampiamente considerati il prossimo grande test per il rally alimentato dall’intelligenza artificiale. Qualsiasi segnale di rallentamento della crescita potrebbe riaccendere i dubbi sulla sostenibilità del boom e delineare l’andamento dei mercati per il resto della settimana. Il titolo è in rialzo dello 0,3% nel premarket. ** "Nvidia è ormai da tempo il barometro dei titoli legati all’IA e la recente scarsa performance rispetto ad altri produttori Usa di semiconduttori è un chiaro segnale dei timori del mercato riguardo al boom alimentato dagli investimenti nell'IA", ha detto Marc Ostwald, capo economista e global strategist presso Adm Investor Services. ** Una riduzione della spesa ciclica e la concentrazione dei flussi di ricavi di Nvidia potrebbero mettere in ombra anche risultati solidi, ha aggiunto Ostwald. ** Se l'azienda comunicasse risultati eccezionali si accentuerebbe inoltre il divario tra i titoli del settore software, che quest’anno hanno subito forti perdite, e quelli dei semiconduttori, che hanno ampiamente beneficiato dell’euforia legata all’intelligenza artificiale. ** Intuit (INTU.O) è in calo del 12,6% dopo che il produttore di TurboTax ha previsto ricavi annuali inferiori alle attese di Wall Street. ** Anche altri titoli del settore software sono sotto pressione: Adobe (ADBE.O) , ServiceNow e Atlassian (TEAM.O) perdono oltre il 2% ciascuno. ** Intorno alle 12.30 i futures E-mini sul Dow sono poco mossi in rialzo dello 0,01%, i futures E-mini sull'S&P 500 sono in calo dello 0,08% e i futures E-mini sul Nasdaq 100 cedono lo 0,23%. ** Gli investitori analizzeranno inoltre i risultati di numerose società del settore dei consumi. ** Nel frattempo, l’Iran ha detto di aver ripreso i colloqui con l’Oman per la gestione dello Stretto di Hormuz, migliorando la propensione al rischio sui mercati. ** I timori relativi a un aumento dei prezzi del greggio sul lungo periodo, all’incremento del debito pubblico e alle aspettative di inflazione hanno spinto i rendimenti dei titoli del Tesoro ai massimi pluriennali la scorsa settimana, per poi arretrare dopo che il Tesoro ha annunciato misure di sostegno. ** L'aumento dei rendimenti aveva penalizzato i titoli tech a inizio settimana, ma il comparto ha poi recuperato contribuendo alla chiusura positiva di Wall Street. ** L'incertezza del contesto macroeconomico e il breve sollievo derivante dalle misure del Tesoro hanno spostato l’attenzione sul discorso del presidente della Fed Kevin Warsh al simposio di Jackson Hole, atteso venerdì, da cui gli investitori sperano di ottenere indicazioni sul fututo percorso della politica monetaria della banca centrale. ** "Una sorpresa 'dovish', incentrata sull’indebolimento della crescita o sui rischi legati al mercato del lavoro, comporterebbe un calo dei rendimenti reali delle obbligazioni e un indebolimento del dollaro, mentre l'azionario potrebbe registrare un andamento positivo", ha detto Kevin Thozet, membro del comitato di investimento di Carmignac. ** "Una sorpresa 'hawkish', con timori espliciti sull’inflazione o la volontà di un rialzo dei tassi, spingerebbe al rialzo i rendimenti a breve termine ... Un discorso che non convincesse gli investitori vedrebbe intensificarsi la pressione sui rendimenti a lungo termine", ha aggiunto.

item.title: Le chef de la CIA s'est entretenu avec ses homologues russes à Moscou, dit le Kremlin
item.description: Le directeur de la CIA, John Ratcliffe, s'est entretenu avec des responsables des services de renseignement russes lors de sa visite à Moscou mardi, a fait savoir mercredi le Kremlin, précisant qu'il n'avait toutefois pas rencontré le président russe Vladimir Poutine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le directeur de la CIA, John Ratcliffe, s'est entretenu avec des responsables des services de renseignement russes lors de sa visite à Moscou mardi, a fait savoir mercredi le Kremlin, précisant qu'il n'avait toutefois pas rencontré le président russe Vladimir Poutine. Le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, a déclaré aux journalistes que Vladimir Poutine avait été informé des résultats des entretiens du chef du renseignement américain, mais a refusé de donner plus de détails. Dmitri Peskov a ajouté qu'il était encore trop tôt pour dire si de tels contacts entre les services de renseignement des deux pays pourraient contribuer à sortir les relations américano-russes de ce qu'il a qualifié de "crise profonde". Le site d'information Axios et la chaîne de télévision américaine CBS News, citant des sources non-identifiées, ont [USN:L8N44M1GS TEXT:"rapporté mardi"] que John Ratcliffe était en visite à Moscou. Il s'agit de la première visite connue d'un patron de la CIA dans la capitale russe depuis le déplacement de William Burns, prédécesseur de John Ratcliffe, pour une réunion avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine en novembre 2021 - soit environ trois mois avant que le Kremlin n'ordonne ce qu'il a présenté comme une "opération militaire spéciale" en Ukraine.

item.title: International Swimming League to resume with London meet in December
item.description: The International Swimming League will return from a five-year hiatus with a one-night All-Star Match at the London Aquatics Centre on December 19, the league said on Wednesday, taking a first step toward its planned full relaunch.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: The International Swimming League will return from a five-year hiatus with a one-night All-Star Match at the London Aquatics Centre on December 19, the league said on Wednesday, taking a first step toward its planned full relaunch. The team-based event will feature some of the world's leading swimmers competing for a record purse, with details to come later, the league said. Past ISL events have featured American Caeleb Dressel, Britain's Adam Peaty and Hungary's Katinka Hosszu. The announcement gives concrete shape to [USN:L1N3XJ07A TEXT:"plans outlined"] by ISL Commissioner Ben Allen last year, when he told Reuters the league hoped to restart in the autumn of 2026 under a revised commercial model less dependent on a single investor and more reliant on sponsorship and media partnerships. The ISL, launched in 2019 to provide a season-long professional competition outside the Olympic cycle, last staged a season in 2021. Its operations were halted after the COVID-19 pandemic and the effects of Russia's war in Ukraine on its principal backer, Ukrainian businessman Konstantin Grigorishin. Allen said in December that the league had initially envisaged a seven-match comeback season across North America and Europe, including at least one event in Asia and possibly another in the Middle East. The ISL had also been considering a one-day format after previously holding competition across two days. In July, the league announced it would pay about 300 athletes [USN:L4N43602V TEXT:"overdue prize money"] owed from its 2021 season. Wednesday's announcement suggests that the London event will serve as a trial of that condensed approach before a wider return. "The All-Star Match is the moment swimming has been waiting for: the world's best athletes, back on the ISL stage," Allen said in a statement. "London is the perfect host city, with a venue built for nights like this and in front of one of the world's great sporting audiences." The Aquatics Centre, built for the 2012 London Olympics, has since hosted major international swimming events. The ISL said it would later announce the swimmers taking part, the match format, ticketing details and broadcast arrangements.

item.title: Airbus employees in Spain resume strike after rejecting offer
item.description: Thousands of Airbus workers in Spain have resumed strike action this week after rejecting the company's latest pay offer and mediation proposal, unions said on Wednesday, ahead of a new mediation meeting scheduled for Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thousands of Airbus (AIR.PA) workers in Spain have resumed strike action this week after rejecting the company's latest pay offer and mediation proposal, unions said on Wednesday, ahead of a new mediation meeting scheduled for Thursday. Unions said about 90% of eligible workers took part in Tuesday's stoppage, which they described as the start of an indefinite strike following 22 days of industrial action in July. French unions briefed on the dispute have said the three striking Spanish unions represent about 40% of Airbus Spain's roughly 14,000 employees. The number of workers taking part could not be independently confirmed. The strike was called after workers voted at plant-level assemblies to reject a pay and conditions proposal presented by the company at a mediation session on Friday. Unions said the offer lacked firm timelines and financial commitments, and deferred key issues such as holidays, flexible hours and transport. Airbus, which is under pressure to meet its annual delivery target of 870 jets, has frozen planned hiring in Spain for the duration of the strike, according to Alfonso Mora, head of the Airbus works council in Spain. Airbus did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Union representatives for UGT and CGT said the stoppage had already slowed military and commercial production and would make it harder for the company to meet its delivery target. Airbus said last week that disruption to administrative and support functions had not yet affected production. Workers are seeking inflation-linked pay rises, the restoration of previous remote-working arrangements and sick-leave benefits. Airbus has already [USN:L6N44I0W2 TEXT:"softened plans"] to reduce remote working following July's protests, allowing staff to continue working from home an average of two days a week, Reuters reported last week. Airbus' eight sites in Spain produce military transport planes and parts for commercial aircraft and satellites.

item.title: China's CNOOC makes record interim profit on higher oil prices, output
item.description: Chinese offshore oil and gas major CNOOC Ltd posted a record first-half net profit on Wednesday, as higher oil prices driven by the Iran war and rising production boosted earnings.
item.dc:creator: Sam Li, Chen Aizhu
item.content:encoded: Chinese offshore oil and gas major CNOOC Ltd posted a record first-half net profit on Wednesday, as higher oil prices driven by the Iran war and rising production boosted earnings. Net profit attributable to shareholders rose 23.4% to 85.8 billion yuan ($12.9 billion) from 69.5 billion yuan a year earlier, according to a filing with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Oil and gas sales revenue jumped 20% to 206.1 billion yuan. The company's average realised oil price rose 23.6% to $85.49 per barrel during the period, while its average realised gas price increased 1.3% to $8 per thousand cubic feet. Net oil and gas production rose 3.7% to a record 398.7 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe), including 275.2 million boe produced in China, up 3.3%. Crude oil and liquids production increased 4.8% to 310.3 million barrels in the first six months of the year, while natural gas output edged up 0.2% to 517.3 billion cubic feet. CNOOC's all-in cost rose to $29.70 per boe in the first half from $28.41 in the first quarter. The company maintained its annual production target of 780 million to 800 million boe and capital expenditure guidance of 112 billion to 122 billion yuan. First-half capex totalled 62 billion yuan. In China, CNOOC made four new oil and gas discoveries, including Luda 16-1 and Qinhuangdao 30-3 in the Bohai Bay, and successfully appraised 16 oil- and gas-bearing structures, including Wenchang 19-3 in the Pearl River Mouth Basin. The company said its onshore unconventional gas reserves continued to grow. Outside China, CNOOC secured three new exploration blocks in Brazil and Indonesia. CNOOC declared an interim dividend of HK$0.94 per share, the highest since its listing. CNOOC's Hong Kong-listed shares closed down 0.8% at HK$24.92, but are up 17% this year, outperforming peer Sinopec, whose shares have gained 0.9%, and broadly in line with PetroChina's 18.38% rise. The benchmark Hang Seng Index has been little changed over the same period.

item.title: China's Jiangsu says it will support pharmaceutical firms' global M&A, licensing
item.description: Chinese biotech hub Jiangsu province pledged to support pharmaceutical companies seeking foreign acquisitions, licensing agreements and joint development projects on Wednesday, as China tightens scrutiny over sensitive technologies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese biotech hub Jiangsu province pledged to support pharmaceutical companies seeking foreign acquisitions, licensing agreements and joint development projects on Wednesday, as China tightens scrutiny over sensitive technologies. Drug development from China-headquartered clinical trial sponsors has [USN:L6N42V0LG TEXT:"grown significantly"] over the past two decades: they ran 32% of all global clinical trials in 2025, up from just 2% in 2009, according to IQVIA, a health sector research firm. Global drugmakers are [USN:L6N3Z903L TEXT:"stepping up"] their search for China‑developed experimental medicines as they cut costs ahead of patent expirations, with industry analysts predicting biotech licensing deals would surge to a fresh record this year. Jiangsu will "support enterprises in participating in global trade and licensing cooperation", the provincial government said in a statement on its three-year plan for promoting development of the local biopharmaceutical industry. In June, China [USN:L1N429033 TEXT:"issued"] sweeping new rules tightening control of overseas deals that involve Chinese investors, technology, data and national security, a month after Beijing ordered Meta to [USN:L1N41A088 TEXT:"unwind"] its acquisition of AI startup Manus.

item.title: Bath & Body Works lifts annual profit forecast as digital demand offsets weak store traffic
item.description: Bath & Body Works on Wednesday raised its forecast for full-year profit and beat estimates for second-quarter results, benefiting from demand for body care products and home fragrances on digital channels.
item.dc:creator: Sanskriti Shekhar, Danielle Kaye
item.content:encoded: Bath & Body Works (BBWI.N) on Wednesday raised its forecast for full-year profit and beat estimates for second-quarter results, benefiting from demand for body care products and home fragrances on digital channels. Younger consumers have prioritized small, affordable indulgences, echoing a "lipstick effect" benefit where demand for nice-to-have products cushions broader spending weakness in a strained consumer environment. Like many consumer companies, Bath & Body Works is in the midst of a turnaround focused on product innovation and enhancing its digital platform under CEO Daniel Heaf. Bath & Body Works posted second-quarter sales of $1.51 billion, edging past analysts' estimate of $1.50 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. "The progress (in its turnaround efforts), because it's early, has yet to offset the changes in the whole business," CEO Heaf told Reuters, adding that the company is seeing a decline in store traffic and a broader weakness in mall traffic. Bath & Body Works has been expanding its distribution beyond its own stores through third-party channels, including Amazon and a partnership with [USN:L6N42U12M TEXT:"Ulta Beauty"] to draw affluent younger consumers. Cosmetics maker Coty (COTY.N) last week [USN:L6N44G18L TEXT:"forecast"] current-quarter earnings below expectations, as consumers become more selective in their spending and higher oil prices also weigh. Bath & Body Works expects annual adjusted profit between $2.60 and $2.80 per share, compared with its prior forecast of $2.40 to $2.65 per share. It benefited from about $80 million in tariff refunds during the second quarter. Excluding that benefit, the company's earnings per share stood at 31 cents. Analysts estimated a profit of 24 cents per share. It forecast a drop in third-quarter net sales of between 2.5% and 5%, compared to estimates of a 2.9% drop. It sees Q3 adjusted EPS between 7 cents and 12 cents, while analysts expect 26 cents.

item.title: Presidente do BC do Japão não participará e Jackson Hole e desvia foco do mercado para o G20
item.description: O membro da diretoria do Banco do Japão Naoki Tamura participará do encontro anual do Federal Reserve em Jackson Hole nesta semana representando o presidente Kazuo Ueda, informou o banco central nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: O membro da diretoria do Banco do Japão Naoki Tamura participará do encontro anual do Federal Reserve em Jackson Hole nesta semana representando o presidente Kazuo Ueda, informou o banco central nesta quarta-feira. Ueda não participará do encontro desta semana devido a conflitos de agenda, informou o Banco do Japão. Não haverá coletiva de imprensa com Tamura durante o encontro, acrescentou o banco. É raro que um membro da diretoria do Banco do Japão participe do encontro de Jackson Hole, que normalmente conta com a presença do presidente ou de um dos dois vice-presidentes do banco central. Ex-banqueiro comercial, Tamura é visto como um “hawk” na diretoria de nove membros e tem defendido publicamente o aumento da taxa de juros para conter os riscos de alta nos preços. O que o novo chair do Fed, Kevin Warsh, possa dizer sobre as perspectivas para a política monetária dos EUA em seu discurso de estreia em Jackson Hole terá enormes repercussões para o Japão devido às oscilações do iene e dos rendimentos dos títulos, afirmam analistas. A ausência de Ueda em Jackson Hole colocará em destaque sua possível participação no encontro de líderes financeiros do G20, organizado pelos EUA na próxima semana em Asheville, na Carolina do Norte. Os participantes do mercado estão atentos a indícios por parte das autoridades do Banco do Japão sobre se o banco central pode acelerar o ritmo e o momento dos aumentos dos juros para lidar com os crescentes riscos inflacionários. Embora o banco central não tenha divulgado se Ueda participará do encontro do G20, o secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, afirmou que está ansioso para se encontrar com ele em Asheville.

item.title: Hard-left presidential candidate's plan to cancel French debt sparks backlash
item.description: France's political class has been roiled in recent years by its attempts to rein in the country's increasingly heavy debt load. Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has a simple but highly divisive idea: cancel it.
item.dc:creator: Leigh Thomas
item.content:encoded: France's political class has been roiled in recent years by its attempts to rein in the country's increasingly heavy debt load. Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has a simple but highly divisive idea: cancel it. Melenchon, of the France Unbowed party (LFI), has revived his calls for the central bank to cancel its holdings of French debt. "All we have to do is take the 18% held by the Bank of France and chuck it in the fire," he has said on the campaign trail. Melenchon has yet to detail his plan, but its central idea is that such an operation would allow France to reduce its headline public debt ratio - now at over 116% of GDP - creating more room for public spending. His unorthodox solution to France's fiscal woes is part of a package of policies that are proving a hit with some voters. A poll on Monday showed Melenchon poised for a run-off with far-right leader Marine Le Pen in next year's presidential election, ahead of mainstream candidates. The idea is not new. Most recently during the COVID-19 pandemic some economists and politicians called for the European Central Bank to cancel government bonds it bought from commercial banks to prop up the euro zone economy. However, such proposals have been rejected in the past, with policymakers arguing that they would lead to a central bank effectively financing a government, which European Union treaties expressly forbid, while also hurting market confidence. Melenchon's latest call is provoking a similar backlash. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, who became France's fifth prime minister in under two years after two of his predecessors were toppled over efforts to tame the deficit, described the proposal as "fraud in its purest form" and warned it would hurt households and businesses. With France needing to borrow record sums, Lecornu warned that even flirting with the idea could spook investors. "If France, which needs to raise 310 billion euros ($361 billion) this year, were to renege on its own signature, who would still lend to us? At best, lenders - if they agree to lend at all - will demand exorbitant interest rates," Lecornu said on X. Melenchon's team did not immediately respond to a request for comment. TAXPAYER ON THE HOOK The Bank of France declined to comment, but its ex-governor Francois Villeroy de Galhau has previously said cancelling government bonds on its books would force France to give up the euro, saddling the central bank with a huge loss that the French taxpayer would have to cover. Not all, however, have balked at the idea. Left-leaning investment banker Matthieu Pigasse, who recently won a mandate to restructure Venezuela's huge debt, backed Melenchon. At the summer conference of the LFI party last weekend, Pigasse said that bonds held at the Bank of France could be cancelled "without any economic or financial impact." His comments sparked a testy exchange on X with former IMF chief economist Olivier Blanchard, who called the debate "idiotic." Blanchard said that if the Bank of France cancelled French bonds, it would no longer earn interest or profits that would otherwise be returned to its sole shareholder, the French state, rendering the move moot in bookkeeping terms while shaking private investors' confidence. While he acknowledged that France's deficit was too large, "proposing false solutions, raising false hopes, is ... irresponsible," he said. ($1 = 0.8572 euros)

item.title: Sterling dips, currency markets look to the U.S. for cues
item.description: The pound dipped from its recent high against the dollar and also slid versus the euro on Wednesday, but with little in the way of major news from Britain, the currency was mainly shaped by broad risk sentiment and developments elsewhere.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The pound dipped from its recent high against the dollar and also slid versus the euro on Wednesday, but with little in the way of major news from Britain, the currency was mainly shaped by broad risk sentiment and developments elsewhere. Sterling shed 0.2% on the dollar to $1.3625, retreating from a six-month high of $1.3675 hit last week. It was at 85.61 pence against the euro, also a fraction softer on the day. , The pound has performed reasonably well among major currencies this year, supported by a resilient UK economy and high British bond yields. These are particularly relevant when markets are calm, as currency markets are at present, as traders focus more on carry trades which profit from rate differentials. It has gained just over 1% on the dollar and nearly 2% on the euro this year. But the focus for currency markets on Wednesday was on moves in the United States. "There is no UK data of note today once again, leaving cable (the pound/dollar exchange rate) to trade off this afternoon's U.S. releases, with Friday's Jackson Hole keynote still the next probable directional catalyst," said analysts at Monex Europe. U.S. PCE, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, is due at 1230 GMT, and could shape expectations for the Fed's interest rate path this year. It will also set the scene for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's speech on Friday at the important central banking conference, which past chairs have used as a [USN:L6N44L0MM TEXT:"high-profile platform to signal policy thinking"] or reinforce existing messages.

item.title: 'Everybody has a Dolly Parton song' - World mourns country music legend
item.description: "It is hard to imagine living in a world without Dolly," Paul McCartney wrote.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: When Dolly Parton tribute artist Brooke McMullen woke up to messages about [USN:L6N44N00S TEXT:"the death"] of the country music star, she thought it was a hoax. Dolly could never die. Parton was "one of those people that you just think is going to be around forever," McMullen said from Brisbane, Australia. "Her loss is huge." Fans across continents, from prime ministers to pop stars, felt the same jolt and flooded social media with [USN:L6N44M16J TEXT:"messages of grief and affection"]. Part of Parton's appeal came from the stories she told in her songs, said McMullen, who takes her tribute show across Australia. "All of her stories are real life and you can connect," she added. "Everybody's got at least one of the songs that they connect to, whether it be that was something that their grandmother introduced them to, whether it be they heard that at a wedding that they went to. Everybody has a Dolly Parton song." 'A GIANT OF AN ARTIST,' SAYS ELTON JOHN Fans said Parton had a rare ability to appeal to audiences across a wide range of political persuasions, age groups, genders and cultures. "Your songs taught us to fall in love and how to express," Uganda's exiled opposition leader Bobi Wine wrote on X. "We will always love you," the rapper-turned-politician added. British pop icon Elton John called her a "giant of an artist" who had the kindest heart. "It is hard to imagine living in a world without Dolly," Paul McCartney wrote. Her songwriting, singing and philanthropy were unrivalled in the world of country music, he added. In Japan, where Parton only toured once in 1979, music figures paid tribute. Seiji Kameda, a prominent music producer and bassist for the rock band Tokyo Jihen, said he had been captivated by Parton's voice since his first year of junior high school. "Her voice shone like the sun and will endure forever. Rest in peace," he wrote on X. 'SHE LIVED LOUDLY,' SAYS AUSTRALIAN PM Politicians praised her contributions to society as well as her music. "I was a huge fan of what Dolly did around literacy around the world," British Prime Minister Andy Burnham told reporters. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Parton made an enormous difference through promoting education and funding hospitals, and that there would be many broken hearts across his country. "She lived loudly, and she lived a great life, and she'll be much missed," he told reporters. McMullen, the tribute artist, said she had a show booked for the weekend, but wasn't sure how she would approach it. Putting on the Dolly Parton wig and sequin dress for shows was always a special moment. "I don't look like Dolly Parton just sitting here," McMullen said. "But it's as soon as you put on all of that and you know, step out onto the stage and everybody is so excited because they just adore Dolly."

item.title: Kremlin diz que diretor da CIA conversou com homólogos russos durante visita a Moscou
item.description: O diretor da CIA dos EUA, John Ratcliffe, manteve conversações com autoridades dos serviços de inteligência russos durante sua visita a Moscou na terça-feira, mas não se reuniu com o presidente Vladimir Putin, informou o Kremlin nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O diretor da CIA dos EUA, John Ratcliffe, manteve conversações com autoridades dos serviços de inteligência russos durante sua visita a Moscou na terça-feira, mas não se reuniu com o presidente Vladimir Putin, informou o Kremlin nesta quarta-feira. O porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, disse aos repórteres que Putin havia sido informado sobre o resultado das conversas de Ratcliffe, que ocorrem em um momento em que a guerra na Ucrânia se intensifica e os esforços para chegar a um acordo de paz duradouro entre os EUA e o Irã estão estagnados. Peskov se recusou, no entanto, a revelar o que foi discutido ou a fornecer mais detalhes. “Tudo o que posso dizer é que houve contatos por meio dos serviços de segurança. Posso afirmar que não houve encontros com o presidente russo. Naturalmente, o presidente Putin é mantido informado de tudo sem demora”, disse Peskov. Questionado se as visitas de autoridades norte-americanas de alto escalão poderiam ajudar a melhorar o estado crítico das relações entre os EUA e a Rússia, Peskov afirmou que os contatos entre as agências de inteligência dos dois países são algo positivo. “Esses contatos muitas vezes continuam mesmo durante os períodos mais difíceis nas relações bilaterais. Nosso presidente, aliás, já falou sobre isso. No entanto, ainda é muito cedo para dizer até que ponto isso, de modo geral, ajudará a tirar nossas relações bilaterais da profunda crise em que se encontram atualmente”, disse ele.

item.title: FTSE 100 flat ahead of US inflation data and Nvidia results
item.description: London's FTSE 100 was muted on Wednesday as a slide in oil prices pressured energy stocks and offset broader gains, while investors awaited key U.S. inflation data and Nvidia's quarterly earnings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: London's FTSE 100 was muted on Wednesday as a slide in oil prices pressured energy stocks and offset broader gains, while investors awaited key U.S. inflation data and Nvidia's quarterly earnings. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) was little changed at 10,875.87 points by 1027 GMT, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) rose 0.3%. Oil prices fell more than $2 a barrel after Iran said it had [USN:L8N44M1SQ TEXT:"restarted talks with neighbouring Oman"] on managing the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran said the discussions covered a "joint temporary navigational corridor" through the waterway and an agreement to clear mines, raising hopes that shipping constraints in the key Middle East route could ease. The decline in crude prices sent the energy sector (.FTNMX601010) down 1.8%, with oil majors BP (BP.L) and Shell (SHEL.L) falling 1.4% and 2.4%, respectively. Luxury retailers (.FTNMX402040) gained 1%, housebuilders (.FTNMX402020) rose 2%, and the travel and leisure sector (.FTNMX405010) advanced 1%. The precious metals (.FTNMX402040) and industrial mining (.FTNMX551020) sectors also rose 1.8% and 1%, respectively, even as metals retreated from recent highs ahead of crucial U.S. inflation data that could offer fresh clues on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate outlook. Software stocks declined, led by a 3.5% fall in Sage Group (SGE.L) . Relx (REL.L) and Experian (EXPN.L) were down between 1% and 1.4%. Investors were also keeping an eye on Nvidia's (NVDA.O) second-quarter earnings later in the day to gauge whether the AI-driven spending boom can continue supporting lofty market valuations. Meanwhile, public inflation expectations in Britain [USN:L8N44M1PI TEXT:"rose"] in August, changing course after falling in recent months, a survey from U.S. bank Citi and pollsters YouGov showed on Tuesday. Among the mid caps, miner Hochschild Mining (HOCM.L) climbed 8.6% after first-half revenue rose 62% from a year ago, making it one of the FTSE 250's top gainers.

item.title: West Nile virus infection causes one death in the Netherlands
item.description: A person has died in a Dutch hospital after contracting the West Nile virus in the Netherlands, the country's public health institution RIVM said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A person has died in a Dutch hospital after contracting the West Nile virus in the Netherlands, the country's public health institution RIVM said on Wednesday. The RIVM reported last week the first West Nile virus infection contracted in the Netherlands since 2020 and said the number of infections that had likely occurred inside the country had now risen to three. It was not immediately clear whether the person who died was one of those previously reported and the RIVM gave no further information on the case. The virus, which mostly spreads to people through mosquito bites, can cause severe, life-threatening illness in about one in 150 people who are infected, according to the World Health Organization. The WHO has said warmer temperatures are giving mosquitoes more time and territory to spread the West Nile virus across Europe, with cases climbing in Greece and Italy this summer. The RIVM said it was still "very unlikely" for people to be infected with the virus in the Netherlands.

item.title: Eight South Koreans missing in Nepal flood, Yonhap News reports
item.description: Eight South Koreans working on a hydropower plant were missing, and 10 others were stranded, following a massive flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border, Yonhap News Agency reported on Wednesday, citing South Korea's Foreign Ministry.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eight South Koreans working on a hydropower plant were missing, and 10 others were stranded, following a massive flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border, Yonhap News Agency reported on Wednesday, citing South Korea's Foreign Ministry. The workers were employed by Korea Energy and Doosan Enerbility Co (034020.KS) , the report said, adding that Nepal has deployed a rescue team to search the affected area. Another 10 South Korean workers affiliated with Doosan Enerbility are stranded in the area and awaiting a helicopter sent by Nepalese authorities to evacuate them, it said. South Korea has established a task force led by the foreign minister and plans to send a joint rapid-response team comprising government officials and fire and police authorities to Nepal as soon as possible, the report said. [USN:L1N44N06K TEXT:"Torrential floods"] in the Himalayan border areas of Nepal and China's Tibet killed at least nine people and destroyed roads, bridges and power projects on Wednesday, as authorities in both countries braced for more casualties and worse damage.

item.title: China's MiniMax sees revenue nearly quadruple in first half as AI demand surges
item.description: Chinese AI startup MiniMax on Wednesday posted a nearly four-fold jump in first-half revenue as demand for its low-cost models and AI platform accelerated, with the company continuing to target cheaper ways to deploy AI at scale.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese AI startup MiniMax (0100.HK) on Wednesday posted a nearly four-fold jump in first-half revenue as demand for its low-cost models and AI platform accelerated, with the company continuing to target cheaper ways to deploy AI at scale. Revenue for the six months ended June 30 rose 283.1% from a year earlier to $116.6 million, reflecting surging demand for cheaper, open-source-based models from Chinese providers such as MiniMax and DeepSeek, which position themselves as lower-cost alternatives to proprietary U.S. systems. MiniMax said it will keep pushing to extend the "performance-cost frontier," first getting performance to a level that can handle complex real-world tasks and then improving efficiency to allow capabilities to be rolled out more widely and affordably. Revenue from its Open Platform and other AI-based enterprise services surged 703.1% to $73.9 million as paying users grew. The segment contributed 63.4% of the startup's total revenue during the period, up from 30.3% a year earlier. Revenue from its AI-native products rose 100.9% to $42.6 million. MiniMax remains a loss-making company, though its half-year loss attributable narrowed to $358 million from $402.2 million last year. MiniMax was one of the "AI tigers" to go public this year, [USN:L4N3Y912W TEXT:"raising HK$4.82 billion"] ($614.86 million) in its Hong Kong listing before its [USN:L1N3YA01E TEXT:"stock nearly doubled on its first trading day"]. The Chinese tech firm also [USN:L4N43C00O TEXT:"raised HK$16.04 billion"] in fresh capital through a share sale and a bond issue last month to fund growth in its AI business. ($1 = 7.8392 Hong Kong dollars)

item.title: Irán y Omán planean establecer un corredor temporal en el estrecho de Ormuz mientras persiste el punto muerto con EEUU
item.description: Irán ha mantenido nuevas conversaciones con su vecino Omán sobre la gestión del estrecho de Ormuz, bloqueado durante casi seis meses de conflicto, y el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Omán se ha mostrado esperanzado en que pronto se pueda anunciar un corredor temporal a través de esta vía navegable.
item.dc:creator: Yomna Ehab, Jana Choukeir
item.content:encoded: Irán ha mantenido nuevas conversaciones con su vecino Omán sobre la gestión del estrecho de Ormuz, bloqueado durante casi seis meses de conflicto, y el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Omán se ha mostrado esperanzado en que pronto se pueda anunciar un corredor temporal a través de esta vía navegable. Irán y Omán han mantenido conversaciones intermitentes durante semanas sobre el control del tráfico a través del estrecho, por el que circulaba una quinta parte de los envíos mundiales de petróleo y gas natural licuado antes de que comenzara la guerra en febrero. Desde entonces, la mayor parte del tráfico marítimo ha quedado paralizado, ya que Irán y EEUU han intentado hacerse con el control de este canal estratégico, imponiendo bloqueos por separado. Irán y Omán afirmaron el martes que habían debatido "un corredor de navegación temporal conjunto" a través del estrecho y acordado desminarlo. "Tengo la esperanza de que pronto anunciemos un corredor temporal para el estrecho de Ormuz y medidas prácticas para restablecer la navegación segura", publicó el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Omán, Badr Albusaidi, en la red social X tras las conversaciones con su par iraní. El presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump —que ha amenazado con bombardear Omán— reiteró una afirmación anterior de que todas las minas del estrecho habían sido retiradas y advirtió a Irán de que no intentara colocar más. IRÁN DENUNCIA LA OFENSIVA DE SANCIONES DE EEUU Aunque las hostilidades activas entre EEUU e Irán se han calmado en gran medida, los esfuerzos diplomáticos para alcanzar un acuerdo de paz se han estancado, y los continuos ataques a buques hacen que el paso por el estrecho de Ormuz siga siendo peligroso. Irán anunció el domingo una lista negra de 45 buques, en un aparente intento de impedir las transferencias de buque a buque que utilizan los productores de energía del golfo Pérsico para eludir el bloqueo iraní. Según algunas fuentes, algunas empresas tienen previsto dejar de utilizar los buques incluidos en la lista negra. En un intento por intensificar la presión sobre la economía iraní, Estados Unidos amenazó esta semana con sancionar a los países que sigan haciendo negocios con Irán, aunque señaló que no impondría sanciones de forma inmediata. Las sanciones no incluían a las instituciones financieras chinas sospechosas de facilitar las exportaciones de petróleo de Irán que el bloqueo estadounidense ha interrumpido. Irán denunció la iniciativa estadounidense de aislar su economía como un acto de "flagrante ilegalidad" y se mostró convencido de que muchos países no se sumarían a la campaña de presión. El miércoles, el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores iraní, Abás Araqchi, subrayó la necesidad de reforzar la cooperación con China durante una reunión con el embajador de Irán en Pekín, según informaron los medios estatales iraníes. Los precios del petróleo caían por tercer día consecutivo, registrando un descenso de más de 2 dólares por barril hasta alcanzar su mínimo en dos semanas, tras los indicios de nuevos esfuerzos para buscar un fin negociado a la guerra que comenzó el 28 de febrero con los ataques de EEUU e Israel contra Irán. A pesar de las tensiones actuales, Estados Unidos está empezando a reincorporar personal a algunas misiones diplomáticas en Oriente Medio que fueron evacuadas o redujeron su plantilla ante la tensión con Irán, informaron a Reuters dos personas familiarizadas con el asunto. Esta medida sugiere que Washington considera que el riesgo de que el conflicto con Irán se agrave a corto plazo es menor, aunque algunas embajadas funcionarán inicialmente por debajo de su capacidad total. EEUU NO TIENE PREVISTO LANZAR NUEVOS ATAQUES POR EL MOMENTO El secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, comunicó a los aliados que EEUU no preveía lanzar nuevos ataques contra Irán por el momento y que, en su lugar, se centraría en otros medios de presión, según Axios. Por otra parte, el Servicio Secreto de EEUU dijo el martes que tenía conocimiento de un vídeo difundido por la televisión estatal iraní en el que se hablaba de un posible complot para asesinar al hijo menor de Trump, Barron. El apoyo de la opinión pública estadounidense a la guerra ha caído a su nivel más bajo desde los primeros días del conflicto, y la popularidad de Trump se encuentra igualmente en mínimos históricos de cara a las elecciones al Congreso de noviembre, según una encuesta de Reuters/Ipsos. Miles de personas han perdido la vida en el conflicto, la mayoría de ellas en Irán y Líbano, mientras que Estados Unidos e Israel han mermado gran parte de la capacidad militar convencional de Irán. Se desconoce el estado exacto de su programa nuclear, que Estados Unidos e Israel pretenden desmantelar. El portavoz del ejército iraní, el general de brigada Mohammad Akrami-Nia, afirmó que se había entregado nuevo equipamiento a las unidades de combate y que la lucha contra dos ejércitos tecnológicamente avanzados había proporcionado a las fuerzas iraníes una importante experiencia en el campo de batalla, según declaraciones recogidas el miércoles por la agencia iraní Mehr News.

item.title: Boston Scientific hit by cyberattack, global operations affected
item.description: Boston Scientific said on Wednesday that a cybersecurity incident had disrupted global operations, including some information systems used to process and ship customer orders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Boston Scientific (BSX.N) said on Wednesday that a cybersecurity incident had disrupted global operations, including some information systems used to process and ship customer orders. The medical device maker said it detected the incident on Aug. 25 and had activated incident-response procedures, working with third-party cybersecurity specialists to investigate and contain the threat. Shares of the company fell 3.5% premarket. Here are some details: The incident is the latest in a [USN:L6N43I17J TEXT:"series of cyberattacks to hit the healthcare sector"], with medical device makers Abbott Laboratories (ABT.N) , Stryker (SYK.N) and Medtronic (MDT.N) , health insurer Clover Health (CLOV.O) , drugmaker Novo Nordisk (NOVOb.CO) and drug-delivery equipment supplier West Pharmaceutical Services (WST.N) among those recently hit. The attack is expected to continue affecting parts of the company's business while recovery efforts are underway, Boston Scientific said. Boston Scientific said it had not determined whether the incident was reasonably likely to have a material impact on its business. An investigation is ongoing, but the full scope and nature of the incident have not yet been determined.

item.title: ICC urges Japan to counter US campaign against court
item.description: Japan should try to counter U.S. efforts to pressure members of the International Criminal Court to quit the body, the Japanese head of the court said on Wednesday, adding that Tokyo's support was pivotal to ensuring the ICC's survival.
item.dc:creator: Kiyoshi Takenaka, Anton Bridge, John Geddie
item.content:encoded: Japan should try to counter U.S. efforts to pressure members of the International Criminal Court to quit the body, the Japanese head of the court said on Wednesday, adding that Tokyo's support was pivotal to ensuring the ICC's survival. The Trump administration ratcheted up its campaign against the Hague-based court last week by [USN:L6N44F14S TEXT:"sanctioning"] its president, Tomoko Akane, and a senior trial lawyer. Washington has said it will also step up efforts to [USN:L6N43F0ZT TEXT:"persuade other countries"] to quit the institution, a call that at least five countries have already heeded. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi initially described the latest move as "[USN:L4N44G0IS TEXT:"very unfortunate"]" but has faced criticism from the opposition, human rights groups and some lawmakers from her own party for not more forcibly defending the court. Speaking via a video link to reporters in Tokyo, Akane called on Japan , the court's biggest financial backer, to help it in its hour of need. 'HIGH EXPECTATIONS FOR JAPAN' "Japan has long made the rule of law a cornerstone of its diplomacy. Consequently, both I and the international community hold high expectations for Japan," she said. "Furthermore, I would like Japan to focus on supporting neighbouring countries that are ICC members, ensuring that they do not succumb to the new U.S. campaign and decide to withdraw from the ICC," she added. The ICC was established in 2002 by the international community to prosecute war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity. The U.S. is not a member. But the court's decision to seek an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a close U.S. ally, as well as a past probe into U.S. troops in Afghanistan has drawn the ire of Washington. Akane said Japan, which joined the ICC in 2007, should leverage its close ties with the United States to dissuade Washington from taking further escalatory measures. "Countries, people and media are saying this is a litmus test for their expectations of Japan ... Japan's strong support for the ICC here will greatly contribute to its future survival," she said. "This is where the real challenge begins."

item.title: Volkswagen, percorso di riduzione costi “non ancora finito” - Ceo
item.description: L'amministratore delegato di Volkswagen, Oliver Blume, ha esortato i lavoratori dello stabilimento di Emden, che potrebbe essere chiuso nell'ambito di un imponente piano di risanamento, a intensificare gli sforzi di risparmio, avvertendo che i costi sono ancora troppo elevati rispetto a quelli dei concorrenti.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'amministratore delegato di Volkswagen, Oliver Blume, ha esortato i lavoratori dello stabilimento di Emden, che potrebbe essere chiuso nell'ambito di un imponente piano di risanamento, a intensificare gli sforzi di risparmio, avvertendo che i costi sono ancora troppo elevati rispetto a quelli dei concorrenti. "Questo percorso non è finito. Perché non ci confrontiamo solo con i nostri risultati passati, ma anche con i migliori siti europei", ha detto Blume al personale, secondo alcuni estratti di un suo discorso diffusi oggi dall'azienda. "I costi del lavoro oggi sono più che raddoppiati rispetto a quelli di siti europei comparabili. E per quanto riguarda i costi di produzione, altri stabilimenti sono ancora significativamente più competitivi. Non è una critica, è la realtà con cui dobbiamo fare i conti", ha detto Blume. Emden, stabilimento dedicato ai veicoli elettrici nella Bassa Sassonia, è uno dei quattro stabilimenti che attualmente non dispongono di un piano industriale oltre il 2030. Blume, che questa settimana sta visitando i siti aziendali nel tentativo di rassicurare i lavoratori e raccogliere consenso sulle ampie misure di riduzione dei costi, ha definito le chiusure come una misura estrema. L’amministratore delegato ha detto ai lavoratori che la responsabilità di Volkswagen non verrebbe meno anche qualora non riuscisse a garantire il futuro del sito. "Lotteremo per le prospettive industriali e i posti di lavoro nelle nostre sedi, insieme ai partner, agli investitori e attraverso nuove soluzioni industriali", ha detto.
